Properties of a naxp

Source: R/naxp.R
naxp_properties.Rd

Get the pattern that a naxp was parsed from, its maximum encoded value and the length of its longest canonical form.

Usage

naxp_pattern(naxp)

naxp_max_encoded_value(naxp)

naxp_max_length(naxp)

Arguments

naxp

A naxp from naxp_parse(), a pattern string or a naxp_encoded vector, whose naxp is used.

Value

  • naxp_pattern(): a single string.

  • naxp_max_encoded_value(): a single integer or double.

  • naxp_max_length(): a single integer.

Details

Encoded values run from 1 to the maximum encoded value with no gaps, which means that the maximum is also the number of distinct non-zero encoded values.

naxp_max_encoded_value() returns

  • an integer if the maximum is less than \(2^{31}\), or

  • a double if it is in the range \(2^{31}\) to \(2^{53}\).

If the maximum is over \(2^{53}\), naxp_max_encoded_value() raises an error, because a double cannot store every integer over \(2^{53}\) exactly. Printing the naxp still shows the maximum.

Examples

postcode_naxp <- naxp_parse(r"(\9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A)")

naxp_pattern(postcode_naxp)
#> [1] "\\9\\9\\9\\9 \\s!! \\A\\A"
naxp_max_encoded_value(postcode_naxp)
#> [1] 6760000
naxp_max_length(postcode_naxp)
#> [1] 7

# An encoded vector can be used in place of the naxp that encoded it
postcodes <- naxp_encode(c("1012AB", "9999 ZZ"), postcode_naxp)
naxp_pattern(postcodes)
#> [1] "\\9\\9\\9\\9 \\s!! \\A\\A"
